hints: Focus on the two separate requirements at once, the shape around the C=C bond and the presence of a chiral centre in the triglyceride part.
Look at the two H atoms on the C=C bond, opposite sides means trans while the same side means cis, so you can quickly shortlist two diagrams.
Consider the middle carbon of the glycerol backbone with its four bonds, it is only chiral when its two $\text{CH}_2\text{O}_2\text{CR}$ ends are different.
walkthrough:
**Check trans or cis at the C=C**

Look only at the left-hand alkene part. Each C of the C=C has one H and one carbon chain.

If the two H atoms are on opposite sides of the double bond, the alkene is trans. If they are on the same side, it is cis.

**Sort A, B, C, D by alkene geometry**

In A and B the H atoms are one up and one down, on opposite sides.

$$ \text{H atoms opposite} \rightarrow \text{trans} $$
In C and D both H atoms are drawn up, on the same side.

$$ \text{H atoms same side} \rightarrow \text{cis} $$
So only A and B can be trans fats.

**Check optical activity in the triglyceride**

Look at the right-hand glycerol part: $\text{R}_1\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{O}_2\text{C}-)-\text{CH}_2\text{O}_2\text{CR}$.

The central $\text{CH}$ is bonded to H, to $\text{OCO(CH}_2)_7...$, to $\text{CH}_2\text{OCO R}_1$ and to $\text{CH}_2\text{OCO R}_1$ or $\text{CH}_2\text{OCO R}_2$.

**Apply the chiral centre rule**

A carbon is chiral and gives optical activity when it has four different groups.

If top and bottom are both $\text{R}_1$, two groups are identical, so the centre is achiral. If they are $\text{R}_1$ and $\text{R}_2$ which are different, all four groups are different, so the centre is chiral and optically active.

Only the trans structure with $\text{R}_1$ and $\text{R}_2$ meets both conditions.

options.A: This has a trans C=C because the two H atoms are on opposite sides, which is correct for a trans fat, but the glycerol centre has two identical $\text{CH}_2\text{O}_2\text{CR}_1$ groups. The central CH therefore has only three distinct groups, is achiral, and the molecule is not optically active.
options.B: This has a trans C=C with H atoms on opposite sides, and the glycerol centre is bonded to H, $\text{OCO(CH}_2)_7...$, $\text{CH}_2\text{OCO R}_1$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{OCO R}_2$. Since $\text{R}_1$ and $\text{R}_2$ are different, all four groups are different, so the central carbon is chiral and the molecule is optically active.
options.C: This has both H atoms on the same side of the C=C, so it is a cis alkene, not a trans fat. It also has two identical $\text{R}_1$ end groups, so the glycerol carbon is achiral and not optically active.
options.D: This does have a chiral glycerol centre because the ends are $\text{R}_1$ and $\text{R}_2$ which are different, so it would be optically active, but both H atoms are on the same side of the C=C. That is cis, not trans, so it is not a trans fat.
